questions.question: Analyse the ethical risks and responsibilities of using technology and social media in social work.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the ethical risks and responsibilities of using technology and social media in social work.
  • a) Confidentiality risks – Possibility of data breaches or unauthorized access.
  • b) Privacy concerns – Clients’ personal information may be exposed online.
  • c) Boundary issues – Blurring of professional and personal relationships.
  • d) Informed consent – Clients must understand digital communication risks.
  • e) Digital divide – Unequal access to technology may exclude some clients.
  • f) Professional conduct – Maintaining appropriate behavior on social media.
  • g) Record keeping – Secure storage and documentation of digital interactions.
  • h) Misinformation – Risk of sharing inaccurate or harmful information.
  • i) Legal compliance – Adhering to laws and ethical codes regarding data use.
  • j) Responsibility – Social workers must use technology ethically to enhance services while minimizing
questions.final_answer: Option Confidentiality risks – Possibility of data breaches or unauthorized access.

questions.question: Critically evaluate the ethical principles embedded in Rights-Based and Developmental models.

  • i) Ethical strength: Balances individual and community development.
  • j) Both models complement each other—ethical practice requires integrating rights protection with
  • sustainable development
questions.final_answer: Option Rights-Based model emphasizes human rights, equality, and justice.

questions.final_answer: accountable

questions.question: Define micro-level social work with an example.
questions.solution_html:
•  Definition: Micro-level social work focuses on helping individuals, families, or small groups to address
  • personal and social problems through direct interaction.
  •  Example: A social worker providing counselling to a person dealing with depression or helping a family
  • resolve conflicts.
questions.final_answer: resolve conflicts

questions.question: Define integrity
questions.solution_html:
•  Meaning: Integrity refers to honesty, transparency, and strong moral principles in professional
  • practice.
  •  Practice: Social workers act ethically, avoid deception, and maintain consistency between their values and
  • actions.
questions.final_answer: actions

questions.question: Explain the value of dignity and self-determination in brief.
questions.solution_html:
•  Dignity: Every individual deserves respect and worth, regardless of their background or condition.
  •  Self-determination: Clients have the right to make their own choices and decisions without undue
  • interference.
questions.final_answer: interference

questions.question: Identify a response to client disclosure of illegal acts.
questions.solution_html:
•  Maintain professionalism: Listen without judgment and ensure a supportive environment.
  •  Follow ethical/legal limits: Maintain confidentiality but report if there is risk of harm to self or others or
  • legal obligation.
questions.final_answer: legal obligation

questions.question: List two components of professional responsibility.
questions.solution_html:
• List two components of professional responsibility.
  •  Accountability: Being responsible for one’s actions and decisions in practice.
  •  Competence: Maintaining proper knowledge, skills, and continuous professional development.
questions.final_answer:  Competence: Maintaining proper knowledge, skills, and continuous professional development

questions.question: Define confidentiality and informed consent in the context of social work practice
questions.solution_html:
•  Confidentiality: Protecting client information and not sharing it without permission (except in legal/ethical
  • exceptions).
  •  Informed consent: Ensuring clients fully understand services, risks, and rights before agreeing to
  • participate.
questions.final_answer: participate

questions.question: Discuss the meaning of social justice
questions.solution_html:
•  Equality and fairness: Ensuring equal rights, opportunities, and access to resources for all individuals.
  •  Advocacy: Social workers work to reduce inequality, discrimination, and oppression in society.
questions.final_answer:  Equality and fairness: Ensuring equal rights, opportunities, and access to resources for all individuals

questions.question: Explain how empathy enhances the effectiveness of a social worker.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Builds trust and rapport with clients.
  • b) Helps in better understanding clients’ feelings and situations.
  • c) Encourages open communication and client participation.
  • d) Improves accurate assessment of problems and needs.
  • e) Leads to more effective interventions and positive outcomes.
questions.final_answer: Option Builds trust and rapport with clients.

questions.question: Describe how personal values can help social workers manage stress ethically.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Provide a moral framework for handling difficult situations.
  • b) Help maintain professional boundaries and avoid burnout.
  • c) Encourage self-reflection and emotional control.
  • d) Promote ethical decision-making even under pressure.
  • e) Support resilience and commitment to professional duties.
questions.final_answer: Option Provide a moral framework for handling difficult situations.

questions.question: Analyse how values relating to the individual influence ethical decision- / making in social work.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse how values relating to the individual influence ethical decision making in social work.
  • a) Respect for individual autonomy guides decisions.
  • b) Promotes non-judgmental attitudes toward clients.
  • c) Ensures fair and unbiased treatment.
  • d) Encourages cultural sensitivity and respect for diversity.
  • e) Helps balance client needs with professional ethics.
questions.final_answer: Option Respect for individual autonomy guides decisions.

questions.question: Describe how the value of dignity and worth of the person influences ethical decisions.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Ensures respectful treatment of all clients.
  • b) Prevents discrimination and stigmatization.
  • c) Promotes client participation in decision-making.
  • d) Supports empowerment and self-confidence of clients.
  • e) Guides ethical actions that protect human rights.
questions.final_answer: Option Ensures respectful treatment of all clients.

questions.question: List the core ethical principles of social work
questions.solution_html:
• List the core ethical principles of social work
  • a) Service – helping people in need.
  • b) Social justice – challenging injustice.
  • c) Dignity and worth of the person.
  • d) Importance of human relationships.
  • e) Integrity and competence.
questions.final_answer: Option Service – helping people in need.

questions.question: Explain the significance of beneficence in ethical social work.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Focuses on doing good and promoting well-being.
  • b) Encourages actions that benefit the client.
  • c) Helps prevent harm or exploitation.
  • d) Guides responsible and caring interventions.
  • e) Strengthens trust in the social worker-client relationship.
questions.final_answer: Option Focuses on doing good and promoting well-being.

questions.question: Explain an ethical dilemma you may face when receiving a gift from a client.
questions.solution_html:
• a) May create boundary issues in the professional relationship.
  • b) Risk of favoritism or bias in service delivery.
  • c) Could affect objectivity and professional judgment.
  • d) Cultural factors may make refusal sensitive or disrespectful.
  • e) Requires following ethical guidelines and agency policy (e.g., politely declining or documenting).
questions.final_answer: Option May create boundary issues in the professional relationship.

questions.question: Critically examine the core philosophical foundations and values of social work. How do these influence ethical practice in real-world settings?
questions.solution_html:
• Critically examine the core philosophical foundations and values of social work. How do these influence
  • ethical practice in real-world settings?
  • a) Human dignity and worth – Every individual is respected, guiding non-discriminatory practice.
  • b) Social justice – Focus on reducing inequality and advocating for marginalized groups.
  • c) Service orientation – Commitment to helping people in need.
  • d) Human rights perspective – Upholds fundamental rights in all interventions.
  • e) Holistic approach – Considers biological, psychological, and social factors.
  • f) Empowerment – Encourages client participation and self-reliance.
  • g) Respect for diversity – Promotes culturally sensitive practice.
  • h) Professional integrity – Ensures honesty and ethical conduct.
  • i) Importance of relationships – Builds trust and effective helping processes.
  • j) Influence on practice – These values guide decision-making, ensure ethical interventions, and help
  • resolve dilemmas in real-world situations.
questions.final_answer: Option Human dignity and worth – Every individual is respected, guiding non-discriminatory practice.

questions.question: Analyse the ethical risks and responsibilities of using technology and social media in social work.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the ethical risks and responsibilities of using technology and social media in social work.
  • a) Confidentiality risks – Possibility of data breaches or unauthorized access.
  • b) Privacy concerns – Clients’ personal information may be exposed online.
  • c) Boundary issues – Blurring of professional and personal relationships.
  • d) Informed consent – Clients must understand digital communication risks.
  • e) Digital divide – Unequal access to technology may exclude some clients.
  • f) Professional conduct – Maintaining appropriate behavior on social media.
  • g) Record keeping – Secure storage and documentation of digital interactions.
  • h) Misinformation – Risk of sharing inaccurate or harmful information.
  • i) Legal compliance – Adhering to laws and ethical codes regarding data use.
  • j) Responsibility – Social workers must use technology ethically to enhance services while minimizing
questions.final_answer: Option Confidentiality risks – Possibility of data breaches or unauthorized access.

questions.question: Explain the principles of social work
questions.solution_html:
• a) Acceptance – Accepting clients without judgment.
  • b) Individualization – Recognizing each client’s uniqueness.
  • c) Self-determination – Respecting clients’ right to make decisions.
  • d) Confidentiality – Protecting client information.
  • e) Non-judgmental attitude – Avoiding bias and prejudice.
  • f) Controlled emotional involvement – Maintaining professional balance.
  • g) Purposeful expression of feelings – Allowing clients to express emotions.
  • h) Professional relationship – Building trust and respect.
  • i) Accountability – Being responsible for professional actions.
  • j) Social justice – Promoting fairness and equality in society.
questions.final_answer: Option Acceptance – Accepting clients without judgment.

questions.question: Critically evaluate the ethical principles embedded in Rights-Based and Developmental models.
questions.solution_html:
• Critically evaluate the ethical principles embedded in Rights-Based and Developmental models
  • a) Rights-Based model emphasizes human rights, equality, and justice.
  • b) Promotes empowerment and participation of marginalized groups.
  • c) Ensures accountability of institutions and governments.
  • d) Risk: May be difficult to implement in resource-poor settings.
  • e) Sometimes leads to conflict with cultural norms.
  • f) Developmental model focuses on growth, capacity-building, and sustainability.
  • g) Encourages self-reliance and long-term solutions.
  • h) Risk: May overlook immediate needs of vulnerable populations.
  • i) Ethical strength: Balances individual and community development.
  • j) Both models complement each other—ethical practice requires integrating rights protection with
  • sustainable development
questions.final_answer: Option Rights-Based model emphasizes human rights, equality, and justice.
